floor_history.headline: Baseline 15; residue localized to cross-jump-store-tail-merge on switch(ret) arms + missing dead-branch-sched lui $v1
Structural mix: shared do_call + shared complete_store dropped 3 stores to sw-source-reg divergence; floor 15->10, 3-insn shortfall remains on per-arm mask hoist.
Structural split-init `var_v1 |=` at complete_store dropped floor 10 -> 6; forces GCC to reuse var_v1's register for final OR while preserving per-arm mask compute.
s4 permuter: 4 legit axes measured dead + fresh-seed campaign converged on Judge-bound split-load-anchor family; both endgame gates fail per 2026-07-27 standing ruling.

Permuter s5: cheat-suppressed random (41k iters) + two exhaustive directed sweeps (288 + 16 combos) all return ZERO improvement over base 235 — the s3 h2a form is a strict local minimum under the legi

Forensics: the 2-insn gap is reorg.c redundant_insn deleting the then-arm lui, enabled by local-alloc giving the else-arm mask constant $v0 instead of target's $v1 — fill-priority hypothesis falsified

Forensics: instrumented cc1 (BB2_QTY_DEBUG) measured local-alloc's quantity table -- the else-arm mask constant is a block-local qty whose range is always disjoint from the counter chain's, so find_fr

frontier.hypothesis: Make the else arm's AND-destination block-local so combine_regs ties the mask constant to it (the measured blk=4 shape), while still producing three distinct store sites, then steer that single tied quantity to $v1.
frontier.mechanism: blk=4 proves combine_regs merges the constant into the and-destination whenever BOTH are block-local, producing target's exact lui/ori/and one-register shape. The blocker today is that the shared complete_store forces the and-destination to be the global var_v1. A form where each else arm computes its mask into an arm-local variable and the OR/store is duplicated per arm (or the shared tail consumes something else) would restore the tie; the remaining question is which register the tied quantity gets -- under the measured rule it would take $v0 unless the counter quantity is allocated first with a covering range, so this must be combined with a reason for the two chains to interleave.
frontier.next_probe: s8 (structural): per-arm block-local mask variable + per-arm OR/store (accept the instruction-count change), measure sandbox --disable all AND the blk=5 QTYDBG line via tmp/grind/func_8006B92C/s7/qty2.sh. The QTYDBG 'got=' value is a faster and sharper oracle than the score: got=3 on the mask quantity is the win condition, and any form that reaches got=3 is worth building out even if its first spelling scores worse.

frontier.hypothesis: Give the else arm a genuine LOAD (2-cycle r3000 latency) in the counter chain so schedule_block has a reason to interleave the two chains, which is the only shape that makes a block-local quantity live across the mask constant.
frontier.mechanism: s7 measured that two 1-cycle ALU chains are always emitted contiguously, so the quantity ranges never overlap. A load in one chain creates a delay the scheduler fills from the other chain, interleaving them; the loaded value's quantity would then be born before the constant and die after it, marking $v0 busy over [birth,death) and forcing the constant to $v1. s5 chassis C already showed a duplicated read of D_800A34F8 is CSE'd away, so the load has to be one CSE cannot fold -- the natural candidate is re-reading the global AFTER a store to it, or reading it through the arm's own already-stored value.
frontier.next_probe: s8: restructure the else arm so the counter is derived from a re-read of D_800A34F8 that CSE cannot fold (e.g. sequence the arm as store-then-read, or derive the counter from the value the shared tail stores), and check the blk=5 QTYDBG ranges for overlap before caring about the score.

frontier.hypothesis: Cross-function check against saEft00Add, the documented coupled fixpoint of the same dual-lui / redundant_insn / unmerged-store-tail trilemma (carried over unchanged from the s6 frontier).
frontier.mechanism: cross-jump-store-tail-merge.md names saEft00Add as BB2's documented instance of this exact residual family. s6 reframed the third leg from 'reorg fill priority' to 'local-alloc register identity for a block-local constant', and s7 has now reduced it further to 'combine_regs cannot tie a block-local constant to a global and-destination'. That sharper statement is directly testable against saEft00Add's much larger accumulated evidence, and any lever found there very likely generalises here.
frontier.next_probe: s8+ (rederive/synthesis): diff saEft00Add's measured levers against this function's s1-s7 kills under the corrected mechanism, and measure on func_8006B92C any lever tried there but not here.
